question: Treatment of invasive intestinal amoebiasis (amoebic dysentery) with metronidazole alone is sufficient and does not require a subsequent luminal amoebiocide.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is false. Metronidazole treats invasive disease (tissue trophozoites in gut wall and liver) but intestinal cysts survive metronidazole. A luminal amoebiocide (diloxanide furoate 500 mg TDS × 10 days, or paromomycin) is mandatory after metronidazole to clear the cyst reservoir and prevent relapse.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct that this is false. Metronidazole targets trophozoites in tissues but does not eradicate intestinal cysts. After completing metronidazole (400–800 mg TDS for 7–10 days), a luminal agent — diloxanide furoate (500 mg TDS for 10 days) — must be added to eliminate intestinal cysts and prevent relapse and transmission.
